svg.text: Sentence "Your journey starts with one step". Row = token id. Highlighted: id 1 = “journey”.
out[b, t, :] picks one token: b = which sequence (0/1), t = token id (0–5), last axis = its features.
Its 4 features are head0’s 2 outputs then head1’s 2 outputs — that is what cat(dim=-1) built.
Both batch slices are identical here only because batch = 2 copies of the same sentence.
Is 2×6×4 the final output? Not in a real model.
GPT stacks many blocks in a loop (x = layer(x)), each running one multi-head attention.
1. Each block must return the same shape it received, (seq_len × d_model) — here (6 × 3).
seq_len is always preserved; d_model is the dimension that isn’t automatically preserved, so it’s on you to control it.
2. Each block also does a residual add x + attn(x), and adding needs equal widths
(same rule as ch2’s token + positional embeddings).
3. But this wrapper widened it to num_heads × d_out = 4 — so (6×4) can’t re-enter the loop or be added
back. It must return to d_model. Two ways:
Option 1 · split: each head makes d_out / num_heads, so concat already = d_model (no extra matrix).
Option 2 · project: keep concat 2×6×4, then matmul each slice by W_o (concat × d_model).
Real transformers do both: split (concat = d_model) + square W_o (d_model × d_model) to mix the heads.
